Digital banking  ·  Lead design  ·  Proposition to MVP  ·  Launched July 2021

Boubyan / Nomo

UK-based Islamic digital banking for Kuwait's globally mobile customers. A regional banking idea that became a live international bank.

The opening

Boubyan set out to become Kuwait's third-largest bank. Domestic growth alone would not get them there, so we looked for a structural shift in customer behaviour, and found one. Affluent Gulf clients were already moving wealth internationally, with offshore demand growing around 9% a year. Opening an overseas account still meant branch visits, heavy documentation and weeks of waiting.

The reframe

Research changed the brief. Customers were largely satisfied with their primary bank and were not shopping for a new one. They wanted international access from the bank they already trusted, so it stopped being an app discussion and became a balance-sheet decision.

The economics only worked at scale, since Kuwait alone could not clear the return hurdle. The target was a platform for the Gulf, with expansion into Saudi Arabia built in, not a product for a single market.

It stopped being an app discussion and became a balance-sheet decision. The insight that reset the proposition

The proposition

The answer was a Sharia-compliant offshore platform that makes moving, managing and growing wealth abroad effortless, without compromising security or trust. It offered fully digital onboarding in minutes, an overseas current account and card, lifestyle-based investing aligned to risk, and a single view across every account from day one, on an architecture built to add lending and mortgages as it scaled.

Shipped outcome

July 2021
Launched by Boubyan Bank Group, operated by UK-regulated Bank of London and The Middle East.
Minutes
To open a UK account in-app, with no branch visit and no paperwork.
6
Currencies offered on the platform today.

Service transformation  ·  Lead service design  ·  Eight-week engagement  ·  Shipped

Workplace injury insurance

An end-to-end claims service for a newly independent insurer, redesigned from ethnographic research through to an implementation roadmap, aligning customers, operations and delivery behind one vision.

The context

A public claims business had just been spun out with a new CEO, board and the ambition to build a world-class experience for people recovering from workplace injury. It inherited mixed capabilities, no delivery track record, and IT provisioning already under way with no clear picture of what to build, while employers, injured workers, case managers, doctors and lawyers all pulled the journey in different directions.

The research

Contextual, observational and telephone research exposed the human cost of a fragmented process. Uncertainty and stigma turned out to be design problems, not soft ones: workers did not want to be seen as the person making a fuss, chased every update themselves, and questioned why an assessor could overrule their own doctor.

The findings set our design principles: relieve emotional distress, reduce uncertainty, and turn the relationship between worker and employer from zero-sum into shared goals. Two personas drawn from real lives kept them grounded.

From insight to delivery

Over eight weeks the work moved from an existing-journey map that made the fragmentation visible, through cross-functional workshops and a proposed future journey, to a service blueprint connecting the experience to the IT systems, skills and processes behind it. It closed with a working mobile prototype and a prioritised roadmap joining design, technology and operating-model change.

From the engagement. Working artefacts, select to enlarge.

Outcome for every stakeholder

Insurer
A stronger financial outcome from operational and process improvement, plus social impact through a better service for injured workers.
Employer
A simpler, more transparent process and less time without cover, thanks to faster, better-planned return to work.
Healthcare professionals
Less time lost to admin through simpler forms and automation, and faster payment processing.
Injured worker
A less stressful experience, faster recovery, and lower risk of injury escalation through a smoother, better-tracked process.

The business case linked better service to lower operational waste, modelled through case examples and benchmarks on deliberately conservative assumptions.

Premium banking  ·  Lead design  ·  Research to proposition  ·  Launched

First Abu Dhabi Bank, Elite

A premium banking experience designed around the whole family relationship, connecting personal service, wealth and digital banking under one proposition.

What customers wanted

Seven insight themes emerged from the research: family legacy, personal relationships, cultural relevance, global citizenship, certified expertise, effortless convenience, and a need to feel genuinely special. Elite customers did not want more product. They wanted a bank that put the relationship first, created premium time, and acted as a safety net for the people they care about.

The proposition

So the proposition put the family at the centre. Alongside relationship-led service and wealth, the digital experience introduced family banking: connected accounts with a shared view, savings-matching between parent and child, and spending simulators that turn everyday trade-offs into progress towards a goal.

Smart controls added per-account spending limits and approved locations, and gamified chores made saving something a family does together.

Shipped outcome

1M+
FAB Mobile Android downloads; 4.1 rating from around 44k reviews.
160+

~60
Consumer-banking NPS in 2021; complaints reduced 5%.

Digital banking  ·  Head of design  ·  Proposition to MVP

Lulo

Colombia's first fully digital bank with a banking licence, designed proposition-out, from the customer offer through every core journey to a complete brand and design system.

One coherent system

Lulo was built from the customer proposition outward. Every major journey was redesigned as one coherent system rather than a set of separate screens: savings and credit, money transfers, the product portfolio, profile management, and help and support.

A foundation to scale on

Underneath sat a full brand and design system: a flexible logo, a type and colour language, an icon set and a component library. This shared foundation let the MVP ship fast and stay consistent as the bank grew across the country.

Shipped outcome

600k+
Customers by year-end 2025.
13k
New customers per month, reported January 2026.
~50%
Of newcomers opened their first-ever savings account with Lulo.

Physical & medical product  ·  Industrial design, interaction & engineering integration  ·  Patented, shipped

NextHaler & Batcane

Making complex technology feel simple and human. Shipped innovation across respiratory healthcare and assistive mobility.

NextHaler, for Chiesi

NextHaler is a next-generation dry-powder inhaler for asthma. The challenge was to fold genuinely complex mechanics into a device that feels effortless: a breath-activated dose mechanism, dependable dose counting and full dose feedback, all behind a simple open, inhale, close. Approved in 2012 and widely distributed across Europe, it won the A' Design Award in the Medical Devices category.

Batcane, reading space through sound

Batcane takes its cue from how bats navigate in the dark. An ultrasonic guide cane for people with visual impairment, it detects obstacles ahead, around and overhead and returns haptic feedback at the fingertips, letting the user build a mental map of the space. The work ran from sketches and CAD through functional rigs to canes produced for clinical trials.

Recognition

How I work

Setting direction and quality, and still designing the work.

Hands-on, at leadership level

I set the direction and the quality bar, build and lead multidisciplinary teams, and still design the critical journeys myself. I stay close to the craft because that is how the standard holds.

At home in regulated complexity

Banking, insurance and healthcare are unforgiving environments. My strength is creating the clarity and consensus needed to move ambitious ideas through the constraints and into delivery and measurable change.

Design tied to the business

I align business, product, technology and operations around one outcome, and make the case in the language leaders decide in: balance sheets, NPV and operating models, not only screens. Work that cannot be delivered is not yet finished design.

Research to roadmap

I'm comfortable across the whole arc: ethnographic research, proposition, service blueprint, prototype, and the implementation plan that gets it shipped. The featured work all reached real customers.
